summary: The gate itself is sound, wired, and strictly better than the *No script yet* it replaces, and its scripts state their limits honestly. Two documents do not. AGENTS.md:167-168 still says the package half is 'closed by construction' -- the exact phrase the backlog cell lists as one of the five falsified claims 'CORRECTED HERE' -- four lines after the same paragraph says the opposite, and io_seam_scan.py:105-107 still says the package enumeration 'ends here rather than growing by one review round at a time' forty lines before the same file says every package a reach can live in must be named. Both are measured false at the staged bytes: javax.sql.DataSource.getConnection() and new javax.naming.InitialContext().lookup() compile clean and pass the gate. Two minors on measured-claim drift (CRC32 vs CRC32C) and a false refusal of java.io types that reach nothing.

findings.title: 'The package half is closed by construction' is FALSE, contradicts its own paragraph, and is the phrase the backlog cell claims was corrected here
The PACKAGES header still claims the enumeration ends here; the same file says the opposite at :146-150 and round 7 plus this round falsified it
findings.failure_scenario:
Read at the staged bytes. io_seam_scan.py:105-107 reads:

  # ... A subclass
  # cannot escape a banned PACKAGE the way it escapes a banned class, so the
  # enumeration ends here rather than growing by one review round at a time.

Both clauses are false and the file knows it. At :146-150, forty lines below: 'IT DOES NOT CLOSE SUBCLASSING *OUT* OF ONE, and an earlier draft claimed it did: review MEASURED java.util.jar.JarFile, which EXTENDS the banned java.util.zip.ZipFile from a package that was not listed, opening a file and passing. java.util.jar and java.util.prefs are listed now, and the honest rule is that each PACKAGE a reach can live in must be named.' And 'the enumeration ends here rather than growing by one review round at a time' was falsified by that same round: the enumeration grew by TWO entries in one review round, and R8-1 above grows it again with javax.sql and javax.naming (measured, compiled, gate exit 0).

This is not a duplicate of R8-1. The same file carrying a claim and its refutation is worse than either alone, because a reader who stops at the comment attached to the PACKAGES list -- which is where you look when adding a package -- never reaches the block at :143. The correction was appended rather than applied to the text it corrects, which is how the round-7 fix left this behind.

Fix: reword :105-107 to the rule at :150 (a banned package closes naming a sibling INSIDE it and nothing more), or delete it and let the :143-157 block carry the whole claim once.

findings.title: Three prose sites state the MEASURED checksum type as CRC32; the measurement is CRC32C
findings.failure_scenario:
MEASURED at the staged bytes: `git ls-files '*/src/main/java/binjava/*.java' | grep -v '^binstore-backends/' | xargs grep -ho 'java\.util\.zip\.[A-Za-z0-9_]*' | sort -u` prints exactly one line, `java.util.zip.CRC32C`. `java.util.zip.CRC32` does not appear in non-exempt src/main at all. The eight java.io types are confirmed correct by the same method.

io_seam_scan.py:153-155 says 'MEASURED: this tree's non-exempt src/main uses exactly eight java.io types and CRC32, and all nine are listed'; :210-212 says 'MEASURED: exactly the eight java.io types below and CRC32 appear in non-exempt src/main, and nothing else'; check-io-seam.sh:20-21 says 'InputStream, ByteArrayOutputStream, IOException and CRC32 live in them and are how every segment in this project moves'; the backlog cell says 'MEASURED as exactly the eight java.io types and CRC32 this tree uses'.

The gate is unaffected -- ALLOWED now lists CRC32C explicitly and the prefix match would have admitted it anyway -- so this does not block. But it is a stated MEASUREMENT that does not match the tree, and it is the round-7 finding fixed in ALLOWED and not in the four sentences that state it. Naming the wrong checksum type in the one project whose segment format is CRC-protected is the kind of detail a future reader copies.
